final_message:
I've built the Étale landing page, but it is **unbuilt and unseen**. There is no `node` binary in this sandbox, so `npm run build` and `tsc` never ran, and I could not render any page or preview. I read the TypeScript by hand and found no type errors. Run `npm run build` first; it is the first handed-over check below.

**Files:** `MASTER.md`, `src/tokens.css`, `src/data.ts`, `src/App.tsx`, `src/App.css`, `src/index.css`, `index.html`, and two throwaway previews: `preview/thesis.html` and `preview/design-system.html`.

**What the page shows:**
- **Hero:** the three slack times for Friday 2 October 2026 at SFB1204 (5:57 am, 10:31 am, 4:17 pm), with a 24-hour strip under them. On the strip, NOAA's four maximum flood and ebb predictions are vertical stems and the slacks are orange ticks. Choosing a time moves a band to that slack's window and states the current before and after it.
- **"Slack is not high or low tide":** the real 6-minute tide curve from 9414290, with the slack times marked on it. A table shows each slack came 10 to 50 minutes after the high or low.
- **Evening alert:** an example alert, labelled as an example and built from that day's figures.
- **Stations:** both stations as the file describes them: where each is, datum, units, and that the cove itself is not measured.
- **Call to action:** one label, "Join the TestFlight beta", linking to `/beta`, in the header, hero and closing section.

Every figure is read from `data/tide.json`; none is typed into the page. There is no temperature anywhere (grep for "temperature" and "°" found nothing).

**Decisions you should check:**
- **The alert copy.** The brief only says swimmers *want* an alert the evening before. The page says "Tomorrow's slack times arrive the night before…", which states it as something the app does. Confirm it does.
- **12-hour times.** The page uses "5:57 am" because US swimmers read times that way. The thesis preview still shows 24-hour times.
- **System font.** No web font is requested: there was no network and nobody to agree to one.

## Theses (UNVALIDATED: headless run)
**Visual thesis:** Étale is drawn as the day of current at SFB1204:
- **Colour:** cold near-black bay-green ground `#0b1513`, fog-pale ink `#dde5e1`, and buoy-orange `#ff6b2c` used only for slack.
- **Type:** the system face (SF on iPhone), very large tabular-figure times, small plain labels, no mono.
- **Layout:** one left edge for all text at a 36rem measure; only the two charts run full width.
- **Components:** flat and sharp, no shadows, 2px radius.
- **First screen:** the three slack times over the full-width day strip, each labelled with date and station, with the beta link beside them. At 375px the times stack, the strip keeps its full width with hour ticks only, and its labels move into a list.

**Interaction thesis:**
- **The one motion:** choosing a slack time (hover with a mouse, focus or tap; 5:57 am is selected at rest) slides a band to that slack's window between its two maximum-current stems. It moves by transform only, 320ms, `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`, with no overshoot.
- **Hover:** a 160ms colour change on controls.
- **Scroll:** does nothing.
- **Forbidden:** scroll reveals, parallax, bounce, looping waves, counting-up numbers, glows, gradients.
- **Reduced motion:** the band moves instantly.

**Allowed patterns:** the hairline zero line (the data axis); the single buoy-orange accent; the dark ground.

**Set aside:** phone-mockup hero with feature cards; bare centred text page; ocean and wave imagery; the printed tide table. **Kept:** NOAA current-prediction trace.

**Brief answers taken as assumptions:**
- **Audience and mood:** swimmers who already read tables; still, cold, exact, before dawn.
- **References:** none were given.
- **Font:** the system face, because no font request was agreed and there was no network.

**Dials:** variance 4 (from "one left edge… strip alone takes the full width"), motion 2 (from "one motion… scroll does nothing"). Density was not sent: the theses do not settle it.

**Design-system lookup:** I kept the 150–300ms hover range and the 375/768/1024/1440 width checks. I dropped the navy and gold palette, Plus Jakarta Sans, scroll reveal, parallax, CTA glow, device mockups, ratings and store badges.

**Bunshin:** not proposed. This brief is a single page, not a whole site.

## Audit: checked here (11 checked, 1 problem found)
**First screen, read from the code:**
- **First screen:** the slack times (`src/App.tsx:190`), the strip (`:206`) and the detail line (`:208`) are all drawn at rest from `useState(0)` (`:163`), with no script needed.
- **Width and edges:** all text is capped at `--measure` (`src/App.css:25-46`); the strip and tide curve take the full width. Every section shares the same edges (`.wrap`, `src/App.css:2`).
- **Narrowest frame:** below 40rem the times stack (`App.css:423`), the chart labels are hidden and a list replaces them (`:430`), and the stems get more height (`:420`).
- **Empty stretches:** none.
- **The one motion:** `.strip-band` (`App.css:191`), with its transform driven by custom properties from `App.tsx:62`.

**Critical**
- **Build not run:** no node in the sandbox. The code was read for type errors, not compiled.

**Important**
- **Alert copy:** it states the evening alert as an app feature, and the brief only says swimmers want one. **This is the one problem:** confirm with the founders or soften the copy (`src/App.tsx:256`).
- **Hover transitions:** the script flags `App.css:129/132/135`. **Not a problem:** each base rule declares its transition (`App.css:64`, `:86`, `:111`); the `.text-link` one was added during the audit.

**Checks with evidence**
- **Thesis against code:**
  - 320ms and `cubic-bezier(0.2,0,0,1)`: `tokens.css:53` and `App.css:197`.
  - 160ms hover: `tokens.css`, used at `App.css:64/86/111`.
  - Palette: `tokens.css:5-13`.
  - System face: `tokens.css:15`.
  - Orange used only for slack: `.slack-time[aria-pressed]`, `.slack-tick`, `.curve-slack`, `.cell-slack`.
  - Nothing reacts to scroll (grep found no scroll listener).
- **Reduced motion:** `tokens.css:56` sets the hover and band durations to 0ms, so the band jumps.
- **Exit animations:** nothing unmounts. The detail line only changes its text (`aria-live`).
- **No layout-property animation:** the script found none; only transform, colour and text-decoration-thickness are transitioned.
- **Focus visible:** every control has a `:focus-visible` outline, and nothing removes the outline.
- **Five states:**
  - Button: all five, with a disabled style written but unused.
  - Slack time: all five.
  - Text link: four; links have no disabled state.
  - Hover is limited to mouse pointers.
- **Tokens, not magic numbers:** all 9 colours are only in `tokens.css`. `index.html` has `theme-color #0b1513`, which is the ground colour, with a comment.
- **Contrast:**

  | Pair | Ratio |
  |---|---|
  | Ink on ground | 14.47:1 |
  | Muted text on ground | 7.04:1 |
  | Muted text on raised blocks | 6.25:1 |
  | Orange on ground | 6.54:1 |
  | Orange on raised blocks | 5.80:1 |
  | Button text on ink | 14.47:1 |
  | Button text on hover colour | 17.22:1 |
  | Axis line | 3.46:1 |

- **Semantics:** the slack times are `<button aria-pressed>`; both charts are `role="img"` with full text labels and decorative parts hidden; the table has a caption and column headers.
- **Exit wrappers and will-change:** none needed (nothing mounts conditionally); no `will-change`.
- **Tells:** the script ran 18 checks with 0 findings. Reading by hand: no fake product drawn in boxes (the alert is labelled as an example), the section layouts vary, no mono, the tone stays plain, and the copy built from data has no em dashes. Inline `left` styles are static data positions; nothing animates them.

## You must run these (UNVERIFIED)
| What to run | Pass condition |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | passes |
| Chrome DevTools > Performance, while switching slack times | no frame over 16.7ms |
| The page at 375, 768, 1024 and 1440px wide | no horizontal scroll; tide-curve labels don't collide around 640–900px |
| The page with the OS reduce-motion setting on | the band jumps instead of sliding |
| On an iPhone, tap each time | the band moves, nothing sticks in a hover state, safe areas are respected |
